findings.source_passage: Throttling his joy, Ahab negatively answered this unexpected question; and would then have fain boarded the stranger, when the stranger captain himself, having stopped his vessel's way, was seen descending her side.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 4, after the exchange of first hails
findings.why_it_matters: 'Throttling his joy' is a characteristically intense Melvillean phrase capturing Ahab's psychological tension; its erasure flattens the moment of the whale-sighting confirmation and loses a key interior beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Throttling his joy, Ahab negatively answered this unexpected question' before the description of the Rachel's captain boarding.

findings.source_passage: "Where was he?—not killed!—not killed!" cried Ahab, closely advancing. "How was it?"
findings.source_locator: paragraph 5, immediately after the captain boards
findings.why_it_matters: Ahab's frantic, repeated cry 'not killed!—not killed!' is interpretively significant—it shows Ahab's obsessive desire that Moby Dick survive to be killed by him alone; erasing it removes a critical character note.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert Ahab's exclamation verbatim after the captain boards, before the narrative account of the prior day's events.

findings.source_passage: "Yes, yes, you relent; I see it—run, run, men, now, and stand by to square in the yards."
findings.source_locator: Gardiner's speech, near end of chapter, after invoking Ahab's child
findings.why_it_matters: This line—Gardiner mistaking a flicker in Ahab's face for relenting and ordering his men to act—is dramatically essential; it shows how desperately Gardiner reads into Ahab, and Ahab's refusal immediately following is all the more devastating. The draft cuts the whole tail of Gardiner's speech.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full closing of Gardiner's speech: '—a child of your old age too—Yes, yes, you relent; I see it—run, run, men, now, and stand by to square in the yards.'

findings.source_passage: she crowded all sail—stunsail on stunsail—after the missing boat; kindling a fire in her try-pots for a beacon
findings.source_locator: long narrative paragraph describing the night search
findings.why_it_matters: The specific detail 'stunsail on stunsail' gives Melvillean texture and urgency to the night search; the draft reduces it to a generic phrase, losing the prosodic and nautical specificity.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'crowded all sail—stunsail on stunsail' in the search narrative.

summary: Three medium-severity findings (loss of 'Throttling his joy,' loss of 'not killed!—not killed!,' and truncation of Gardiner's climactic speech) and one low; no single high-severity failure, so the draft passes but should be strengthened in regeneration.
